item.title: Cristian Espinoza: San Jose's star turns Nashville's missing piece
item.description: Cristian Espinoza: San Jose's star turns Nashville's missing piece By Justin Ruderman Nashville SC's Cristian Espinoza: Family, sacrifice & legacy After seven sensational seasons with the San Jose Earthquakes , Cristian Espinoza has finally lifted his first MLS trophy in Nashville with the 2026 Supporters' Shield. The 31-year-old Argentinian enjoyed many memorable moments in San Jose, becoming the club's all-time leader in assists while earning two MLS All-Star selections (2023, '25). But ahead of the 2026 season, it was time for a change. "It was a decision that was pondered for a long time," Espinoza explained in Breakaway presented by AT&T . "It was also about weighing what I wanted for my career, and also weighing up the hardest part for me, the family aspect. "My family was comfortable in San Jose and I think that was the hardest part, taking away their comfort, their stability, for something that I perhaps needed and wanted, which was a change. I have no doubt that this great sacrifice is worth it." It didn't take long for that choice to pay off, as Espinoza hit the ground running in Nashville, leading the team with 14 assists so far this season. Alongside fellow Designated Player attackers Hany Mukhtar and Sam Surridge , Espinoza forms arguably the league's most fearsome attacking trio, combining for an astonishing 63 goal contributions so far in 2026 while helping Nashville claim their first Supporters' 'Shield . With the MLS single-season points record and MLS Cup presented by Audi still within reach, that could spell even more history for Espinoza and the Coyotes. "At this point I don't really care [about] my personal numbers in terms of assists or goals," said Espinoza. "I just really want to help the team to be on the next level and to achieve more trophies." Espinoza and Nashville continue to chase the MLS single-season points record of 74 set by Inter Miami CF in 2024 when they host the Philadelphia Union on Wednesday night (8:30 pm ET | Apple TV ).

item.title: Another Texas high school football team cancels season amid mounting injuries
item.description: Another Texas high school football season has come to an early end. Meridian is forfeiting its final two games as injuries take a toll on its roster. (RobMattingley/Getty Images/iStockphoto) Another Texas high school football team has ended its season early as injuries and declining participation affect programs across the state. Meridian High School, about 70 miles south of Fort Worth, announced Wednesday that it would cancel the rest of its football season because of mounting injuries, according to Chron . The Yellow Jackets, who compete in Class 2A Division II, finished 1-7 and will forfeit their final two games against Santo and Mart. "This was an extremely difficult decision and one that was not made lightly," Meridian head coach and athletic director Jim Kerbow said in a statement. "The safety and well-being of our student-athletes must always come first." Meridian had been outscored 96-0 in its previous two games against Crawford and Frost. The district also canceled its junior high football season in September because of low participation. Meridian joins several Texas schools, including Austin's Liberal Arts and Science Academy, Keene, Baird and Grapeland, that have canceled seasons or forfeited multiple games amid injuries or low roster numbers, according to Chron. The cancellations come amid declining youth tackle football participation nationwide. Participation among children ages 13 to 17 fell 2.9% from 2019 to 2025, while participation among children ages 6 to 12 dropped 6.9%, according to the Aspen Institute's Project Play. Despite the disappointment, Kerbow said protecting players remains the district's top priority. "We are proud of the effort they have given to Meridian football," he said. item.title: DFB-Pokal: Dresden advance as Schalke's second round curse continues
item.description: DFB-Pokal: Dresden advance as Schalke's second round curse continues Two second-half goals secured a cup victory for Dynamo Dresden against goal-shy Schalke. The lack of clear chances at either end reflect the form of the poor form of the clubs in their respective leagues. Dresden started the game on the front foot, but they failed to keep that up in an uneventful half of football. Hee-Chan Hwang's header, which was easily dealt by Lennart Grill, was the only chance Bundesliga's lowest-scoring side created in the first-half. However, the second-half started with the hosts breaking the deadlock through 19-year-old Patric Covic. Schalke improved after going a goal behind, but they couldn't find a way to beat the excellent Grill in Dresden's goal. And the result was sealed when fan favorite Christoph Daferner doubled the hosts’ advantage with a free header from a corner-kick by fellow substitute Alexander Rossipal. The 2. Bundesliga side reached the Round of 16 in the cup for the first time since the 2014/15 season, in which they also knocked out Schalke from the competition. The five-time champions knocked out from the cup in the second round in each of the last six seasons, with four of them coming against teams from lower divisions. Dresden will next face Hannover in a 2. Bundesliga fixture between two teams currently in the relegation zone. Schalke play against RB Leipzig and TSG Hoffenheim in Bundesliga before November's international break.

item.title: Week 8 IDP Fantasy Football Rankings: DeForest Buckner Being Traded Could Shift The Landscape
item.description: San Francisco 49ers defensive tackle DeForest Buckner (99) during minicamp at the SAP Performance Facility. Mandatory Credit: Stan Szeto-USA TODAY Sports | USA TODAY Sports It feels like in a blink of an eye we went from drafting our fantasy football teams to reaching Week 8. It's almost Thursday again, so we need to get our lineups set for the upcoming week. While most fantasy football players only have to focus on players on the offensive side of the ball, IDP players have to focus on every player who takes the field. While starting individual defensive players makes fantasy football a lot more fun, it also makes it a lot more difficult. Not only are there twice as many players to keep track of, but it's twice as difficult to get information on them because everyone wants to focus on offense. That's where we come in. We are going to make sure you have the right players in your lineups this week. These are our fantasy football IDP rankings for Week 8. IDP Linebackers These are the players who score the most points on the defensive side of the ball. Their tackling gives them the safest floor, while their ability to rush the quarterback, force fumbles, and play the pass gives them massive upside and different ways to score fantasy points. The linebackers with high tackle numbers will always be up near the top of the rankings. Edge rushers do hold some value as linebackers, but are much more valuable as defensive linemen. Defensive Linemen Linemen have the lowest floor, but they do have a ton of upside. On any given play, they can get a sack, forced fumble, fumble recovery, which can go a long way in helping you win your week. The issue is there aren't a ton of defensive ends who are consistent high-end producers. That's why an elite defensive lineman might be the most valuable piece on any IDP team. Defensive Backs Defensive backs tend to be the least consistent of any defensive position, but there are some who give you consistent tackle numbers. However, interceptions can skew their week drastically, and they are nearly impossible to predict. Safeties are usually more valuable than cornerbacks, but corners have closed the gap a bit in recent years. Especially now that slot corners have become more of a defensive staple in the NFL. item.title: Cristiano Ronaldo beats Lionel Messi to ‘BOAT’ award
item.description: Cristiano Ronaldo beats Lionel Messi to ‘BOAT’ award Real Madrid legend Cristiano Ronaldo has staved off stiff competition, to scoop the award for the ‘Greatest Ballon d’Or of all time’. As much was made official on Wednesday. The 2026 Ballon d’Or ceremony of course took place earlier this week, with the name of Bayern Munich frontman Harry Kane ultimately etched into the history books. All the while, though, votes were being counted for a separate fan prize, in the form of ‘The BOAT’. This saw some of the greatest Ballon d’Or-winning campaigns ever pitted against one another, in a vote to decide which should be considered the very best. Cristiano Ronaldo and Lionel Messi inevitably dominated the shortlist, having racked up 13 ‘Golden Balls’ between them. And as alluded to above, despite the latter having racked up three more such awards over the course of his glittering career, it is Ronaldo who has secured for himself the ‘BOAT’. The Portuguese’s iconic 2008 win has been named the greatest Ballon d’Or year ever, followed by Messi in 2012 in 2nd place. Conor Laird – GSFN

item.title: LeBron James’ early absence highlights the Philadelphia 76ers’ veteran workload management
item.description: Source: headlinephotos/Depositphotos LeBron James’ first absence has highlighted Philadelphia’s approach to managing its veteran players. The 41-year-old forward missed the October 24 game against Milwaukee for lower back and sciatica management. He returned the following night as Philadelphia suffered its first defeat of the 2026 NBA season. The 76ers lost 106-93 to Detroit while several rotation players were unavailable. James scored 18 points and started at center because Philadelphia lacked several frontcourt options. The opening week showed how player availability can affect the team’s lineup and defensive assignments. LeBron James’ absence changes Philadelphia’s rotation LeBron James missed Philadelphia’s October 24 victory over Milwaukee for lower back and sciatica management. He had played 34 minutes against New York and 33 against Cleveland. The Milwaukee game was the first of 2 consecutive games for Philadelphia. Coach Nick Nurse adjusted his rotation while James rested. Dean Wade started in James’ place after missing the opening 2 games with an ankle injury. Tyrese Maxey and other teammates took on additional ball-handling responsibilities during the matchup. Philadelphia defeated Milwaukee 127-116 to improve to 3-0. Joel Embiid recorded 28 points, 11 rebounds, and 10 assists during the victory. The result gave Philadelphia an early example of how its other starters could contribute without James. Philadelphia 76ers manage LeBron James’ playing time LeBron James entered his 24th NBA season after dealing with sciatica during the previous campaign. The condition had kept him out of the Lakers’ first 14 games in 2025. His back remained part of Philadelphia’s injury management during the opening week. James played 34 minutes against New York and 33 against Cleveland. He averaged 15.5 points, 9.5 rebounds and 6 assists in those appearances. Philadelphia then rested him for the opening game of its consecutive weekend matchups. James turns 42 on December 30, 2026. Coach Nick Nurse has discussed managing playing time for James and Joel Embiid. The team’s early rotation decisions reflect that approach as Philadelphia balances veteran availability with its regular season schedule. LeBron James contributes across Philadelphia’s opening victories James made his Philadelphia regular season debut against New York on October 20. He recorded 14 points, 9 rebounds, and 7 assists. The 76ers defeated the defending NBA champions 106-100 at Madison Square Garden. His next appearance came against Cleveland on October 22. James contributed 17 points, 10 rebounds, and 5 assists. Philadelphia overcame a 29-point deficit to win 114-106. Tyrese Maxey scored 28 points in the opening victory against New York. James contributed through rebounding and passing while sharing offensive responsibilities with his new teammates. item.title: Former Man City star insists Lamine Yamal should have won Ballon d’Or: ‘What are basing this on?’
item.description: Former Man City star insists Lamine Yamal should have won Ballon d’Or: ‘What are basing this on?’ The 2026 Ballon d’Or panned out in the worst possible manner for Barcelona, who only had Lamine Yamal’s Kopa Trophy to cheer for in terms of individual awards in men’s category. Other than that, Yamal finished third behind Kylian Mbappe and Harry Kane, who eventually won the Ballon d’Or after an extraordinary season with Bayern Munich. Many believe Yamal was robbed for not being given the Ballon d’Or and one of them is none other than former Manchester City star Samir Nasri. Nasri’s assessment of Ballon d’Or Speaking on a French podcast, Nasri made no secret of his displeasure at the outcome, insisting the award belonged to Barcelona’s Lamine Yamal. “ I absolutely disagree with Harry Kane winning it,” he said (h/t Diario SPORT ). Yamal finished third in Ballon d’Or 2026. (Photo by Gareth Cattermole/Getty Images) “He’s not even the best player in the Bundesliga, that’s Olise; nor was he England’s best player at the World Cup. The winner should have been Lamine Yamal.” The former midfielder went on to question the very criteria behind Kane’s triumph, downplaying the England captain’s goalscoring exploits in Germany. “What are we basing this on? Just on the goals scored? He wins a league in which he practically plays alone,” he added. To underline his point, Nasri reached for a pointed comparison, even at the expense of French football. “It’s like if Ferran Torres scores 50 goals with PSG, wins Ligue 1, the Coupe de France and is given the Ballon d’Or,” he said. Nasri believes Yamal is integral to Barcelona and should have won the Ballon d’Or. (Photo by Gareth Cattermole/Getty Images) Why Nasri rates Yamal so highly At the heart of his argument was the sheer importance of Yamal to Barcelona, something Nasri felt set the teenager apart from his rivals. “Yamal is the engine of Barça, he’s his club, his team!” he said. To reinforce that view, the former City man drew a contrast with Mbappe’s time in Paris, suggesting the Frenchman never held the same status at his club. “When he was at PSG, it was Neymar’s team! Regardless of the titles, it was still Neymar’s team! ” he concluded.

item.title: 5-star C Lewis Uvwo commits to Providence
item.description: Five-star center Lewis Uvwo has announced his commitment to Providence, becoming the first top-10 overall recruit to pledge to the Friars under head coach Bryan Hodgson . The 6-foot-11 senior out of Prolific Prep ultimately chose Providence over Kentucky, Baylor, and Cal, but received offers from North Carolina, Michigan, BYU, Duke, and more. [ $19.99 gets you a FULL year of On3 | Rivals national coverage ] Uvwo, originally from Nigeria, is ranked as the No. 7 overall recruit in the 2027 class, the No. 1 ranked center, and the No. 4 player in Florida, according to the Rivals Industry Rankings , an average of all three major recruiting media companies (Rivals, ESPN, 247Sports). Uvwo was one of the biggest risers in the country this summer, climbing from the top-50 into the top-10 nationally. He was named EYBL Defensive Player of the Year after averaging 5.1 blocks per game. Scouting Uvwo Rivals National Recruiting Analyst Jamie Shaw has evaluated Lewis Uvwo multiple times in person, recently writing this about his game: Not often are we able to watch a player dictate the flow of a game without having to touch the ball on the offensive end of the floor. This is the type of defensive dominance that we saw from Lewis Uvwo this summer. His unique combination of length, twitch, timing, and tenacity forced teams to game plan for him and know where he was on every possession. Uvwo has excellent timing, both hands, and that anticipation leads to his ability to quickly close angles. His twitchy athleticism is also interesting in his ability to slide and turn his hips at pace. He seems to enjoy playing defense. He smiles as he blocks a shot and looks at the shooter with puzzled dismay. Offensively, Uvwo plays a basic game right now. Most of his buckets come from putbacks, rim runs, and lobs from the dunker spots. He has not shown much range or an ability to create advantages (by passing or scoring) with the ball in his hands at this point. The defensive presence is unique, and it is something that sets him apart from his peers in this class.

item.title: Real Madrid defender silences critics with starring display against Barcelona
item.description: Real Madrid defender silences critics with starring display against Barcelona There was a lot at stake when Real Madrid visited Barcelona this past weekend, including prestige as well as the La Liga title race. The stakes were arguably higher for the Real Madrid defence, which has fallen prey to Barcelona’s outstanding attack multiple times in the recent past. Naturally, all eyes were on the Real Madrid backline, and especially Dean Huijsen, who has built a reputation of sorts for faltering against big teams. But that wasn’t the case against Barcelona. Huijsen’s performance vs Barcelona As reported by MARCA , Huijsen has truly silenced the critics pointing at his lack of performance against big teams by pulling off a brilliant display vs Barcelona. Huijsen has been mightily impressive so far. The numbers back up the eye test, with Huijsen finishing the game with 10 clearances, 16 defensive actions and four blocks. More importantly, he was excellent with the ball. The centre-back completed 37 of his 45 passes at 83% accuracy, seven of which broke lines, and his composure on the ball helped Real Madrid play through Barcelona’s intense press at key moments. Difficult outings at the Metropolitano in both 2025 and 2026, coupled with an inconsistent debut campaign that cost him a World Cup place, had fuelled genuine doubts about his big-game temperament. Thanks to this performance, Huijsen has firmly hit back at his critics. Mourinho’s role in Huijsen’s transformation Mourinho and Huijsen have worked together in the past. (Photo by Fran Santiago/Getty Images) Much of the credit for his resurgence has gone to Jose Mourinho. The Portuguese has placed clear demands on the centre-back, prioritising defensive solidity and aggression without stripping away the ball-playing qualities that make him so highly rated. Huijsen looks increasingly comfortable in a system built on concentration, intensity and competing on every single play. There is still room for growth, but he is beginning to translate his natural talent into consistent, complete performances. That improved form also strengthens his standing within the squad. With Eder Militao still working back to full fitness, the partnership of Ibrahima Konate and Huijsen is emerging as Mourinho’s preferred pairing. The Clasico validated that choice and handed the Spaniard the perfect platform to cement his place heading into an important phase of the season.

item.title: Prem eyes English expansion despite Welsh interest
item.description: Cardiff faced Northampton in the Heineken Champions Cup earlier this month [Getty Images] English rugby bosses have confirmed they are concentrating on expanding the Prem with English clubs rather than bringing in teams from Wales. Prem Rugby, which runs the English top flight, has released a joint statement alongside the Rugby Football Union (RFU) stating they were looking at adding two English clubs by 2029. This came after reports the Welsh Rugby Union (WRU) has expressed an interest in joining an Anglo-Welsh league. The Professional Rugby Board (PRB), which runs the professional game in Wales, met on Wednesday and were told the WRU plans to explore a future in the English club game. While senior sources in English club rugby have confirmed interest from the WRU, they insist negotiations are not taking place. What English bosses say The Prem has been reduced to 10 sides after Wasps, Worcester and London Irish were forced to fold during the 2022-23 season. Traditional promotion and relegation to and from the top tier has been scrapped from the start of the 2026-27 season after landmark changes to English rugby were voted through. Instead of earning a play-off shot at replacing the Prem's bottom side by finishing top of the second-tier Champ and meeting the top flight's minimum standards, clubs will instead apply to join and be judged across a range of criteria. Bids will be assessed on standard of play, finances, investment potential, infrastructure and how their geographical base could help spread the Prem's appeal, among other factors. The league hopes to initially expand to 12 teams for the 2029-30 season with a "long-term ambition" to grow further. Conditions were initially set that any team wanting to play in the Prem will need to complete a campaign in the Champ before being considered. A joint Prem Rugby and RFU statement said: "Prem Rugby and the RFU are committed to expanding the English top-flight, with a provisional target season to grow to 12 teams by 2029-30. "The Prem is an attractive league and responsibility for its expansion sits with the Men's Professional Rugby Board (MPRB), which has established detailed entry criteria that any prospective club would need to satisfy. "Resources are currently focused on supporting English clubs throughout the pyramid who aspire to join the league." The RFU would have to approve Welsh teams moving into the league due to it becoming a cross-border competition. What the WRU say Wales have four professional sides, Ospreys, Cardiff, Scarlets and Dragons, that currently play in the 16-team United Rugby Championship (URC) which includes teams from Scotland, Ireland, Italy and South Africa. Welsh rugby's governing body, along with the other national unions, are stakeholders in that league. item.title: Mark Walter Definitively Answers if He’ll Sell the Dodgers
item.description: Los Angeles Dodgers owner Mark Walter assured Dodger fans he has no plans to sell the Dodgers after selling some of his biggest sports assets. Walter, over the past year, sold his stakes in the Los Angeles Lakers and Chelsea FC and is currently looking to sell the Los Angeles Sparks . These sales came about during a federal probe into potentially fraudulent loans from his insurance companies to other companies which he owns. MLB commissioner Rob Manfred also stated the league is looking into Walter’s situation. “As always when we have an investigation, external law enforcement, whatever, we monitor that and that’s where we are right now,” Manfred said. Walter didn’t comment on the investigation, but made clear his intentions for the Dodgers. “We’re going to keep the team no matter what,” Walter said. “We’re going to be winning for 10 years or more. I think our commitment to do so will be just like it has been in the past. And, you know, we don’t win every year, but we’re going to try to.” Oct 17, 2025; Los Angeles, California, USA; Los Angeles Dodgers owner Mark Walter reacts after game four of the NLCS round for the 2025 MLB playoffs against the Milwaukee Brewers at Dodger Stadium. Mandatory Credit: Kirby Lee-Imagn Images Will the Federal Investigation Affect the Dodgers? While the probe into Walter’s dealings could derail the Dodgers’ success, Walter has no intention of putting the brakes on for the Dodgers. They’ve been extremely successful under his ownership, and he doesn’t anticipate any change in the team’s success going forward. “I certainly hope we can look forward to winning another World Series next year under my ownership,” Walter said . “And I think we’re just trying to win consistently, and do so for not just next season, but for the next decade and decades beyond that.” He also sent a message to the fans after the Dodgers’ loss in the NLCS, saying their ambitions haven’t changed. “I really hope that the fans feel how much we appreciate them, because we’re all fans too,” Walter said . “And this [year] was a kind of bad end to the season for us. But you’ve got to look at how we’ve done every year and really realize they’re gonna come back and support us again next year, because we’re going to be out there fighting again for a World Series.” Regardless of Walter’s situation, the Dodgers are sure to contend for a World Series next season, and will hope to bring a championship back to LA regardless of their outside circumstances.

item.title: Dan Campbell compares Lions' fourth-down approach to this John Candy movie prop
item.description: ALLEN PARK — Detroit Lions coach Dan Campbell was asked on Wednesday, Oct. 28, about his fourth-down decision against the Green Bay Packers for the third straight media session, and now he might have put it into terms that stick. Emphasis on might. When asked about the aggression that's become his calling card — and inspired other coaches around the league to follow suit — Campbell said he thinks of his trademark move a bit like the fedora that John Candy wears in the 1989 flick "Uncle Buck." "I think it's just part of my flavor, what I believe in a little bit," Campbell said. "Have you guys ever seen 'Uncle Buck'? I think I'm a little bit like his fedora, the hat that he wears, right? It's a little bit of flavor and it's my favorite hat, but just the mere sight of it really bothers a lot of people. "So, I always think of Uncle Buck a little bit, when John Candy's wearing that. 'Is it the hat?'" More: Lions safety Kerby Joseph returns to practice Campbell has made many high-profile fourth-down decisions. Some have worked — like in the 2024 meeting with Green Bay, when Detroit secured a first down to burn the rest of the clock before kicking a game-winning field goal — and some haven't — like the 2023 NFC Championship. He'll take the good with the bad. And even though Sunday's strategic move didn't yield a first down, it ultimately led to a victory, as the Lions nearly had a full four minutes to move downfield and allow Jake Bates to kick a field goal as time expired. "Anyway, but I get it. And listen, everybody's different, and it doesn't mean right, wrong. It's like I said the other day: it's really what you believe in and there's no right or wrong," Campbell said. "It's what you really believe is going to help you win the game per that week, per that opponent." In any case, it's safe to assume that this won't be the last debate over a fourth-down decision during Campbell's tenure as Lions coach. nbianchi@detroitnews.com @nolanbianchi This article originally appeared on The Detroit News: Dan Campbell compares Lions' fourth-down approach to this John Candy movie prop

She is currently tied with Hall of Fame boxer Christy Martin at 32 total knockouts. “Boxing has been my life, and I never could have imagined the journey it would take me and my family on,” said Serrano as part of Wednesday’s announcement, recalling her early days when women’s boxing was still fighting for any recognition in small theatres to headlining Madison Square Garden in New York in front of a sold-out arena. “Jordan (Maldonado, her trainer) and I always believed, and I’m proud of everything we’ve accomplished,” said Serrano, but made it clear it didn’t happen without support. “Nakisa, Jake and MVP believed in me and in women’s boxing, and together we’ve helped change what’s possible for women in this sport. We’ve fought for respect, equal opportunities, fair pay, and the choice to compete under the same rules as men. There’s still more work to do, and I’ll continue fighting for the next generation long after I hang up my gloves.” In her last fight as the main event of MVPW-03 in May 2026, Serrano tied the all-time women’s boxing record previously held by Christy Martin with her 32nd professional knockout against top contender Cheyenne Hanson. With two records left to break as her goal before retiring, Serrano headlined the first-ever championship boxing event on TikTok LIVE and the first-ever unified women’s world championship contested over 12 two-minute rounds in August 2026 in Temecula, California.
